provinces.name: Saraleon
provinces.notes: The Golden City on the Golden Strait (capital landmark).

settlements.name: Velkgorod
settlements.notes: relicHolder:moonScales; The great river-market of the Velkar, where every bale and ingot is weighed on the Moon-Silver Scales kept in the merchants' guild-house. Northern traders, steppe horse-dealers and Saraleonese factors all trade under one market law, and quarrels go before the scale-keeper rather than the prince.

settlements.name: Ustrinsk
settlements.notes: Harbour at the mouth of the Ozerka, where seagoing ships unload into river boats bound for Velkgorod. The harbour-reeve is paid by Velkgorod's merchants and does not pretend otherwise.

settlements.name: Nevodny
settlements.notes: Seine-net fishers on the east shore of Lake Ozerna; their catch is on Velkgorod's market tables by noon.

settlements.name: Medosk
settlements.notes: Forest village of wild-hive beekeepers. Medosk honey and mead go downriver as far as the Golden City.

settlements.name: Krutin
settlements.notes: Bluff-top village at the head of the northern bay. Its watchers light a signal fire when strange sails come up the Gray Firth.

settlements.name: Ozerny
settlements.notes: Lake-country town and the trappers' winter market. The headman keeps every trapper's debt on notched tally-sticks, and nobody has ever seen him lose one.

settlements.name: Kunagrad
settlements.notes: Fur-market on the Gray Firth coast, where marten and sable are traded to northern ships for iron, salt and silver.

settlements.name: Sobolny
settlements.notes: Sable-trappers' village on the cold north shore; its pelts fetch the best prices in Velkgorod.

settlements.name: Zhuravsk
settlements.notes: Village among coastal reed-beds where cranes nest each spring; the villagers count the returning birds to judge the year.

settlements.name: Zamorsk
settlements.notes: Landing-place for traders from over the sea. A Hvarn family has kept the guest-hall here for three generations and speaks for the northerners in Velkar disputes.

settlements.name: Volokgrad
settlements.notes: Palisaded town at the head of the Volok, where boats are hauled out onto log rollers for the drag south. The dragmasters' guild sets the toll and the order of passage, and a bribe moves a crew up the queue.

settlements.name: Plotny
settlements.notes: Raftsmen who float timber down the coast to Ustrinsk.

settlements.name: Strugin
settlements.notes: Boatwrights on the Ozerka who build light river boats that six men can drag over the Volok.

settlements.name: Zverin
settlements.notes: Trappers' hamlet at the edge of the eastern marsh-forest.

settlements.name: Smolin
settlements.notes: Tar-burners' town on the Borova. Every karvi on the rivers is pitched with Smolin tar, and the whole town smells of it.

settlements.name: Zavolny
settlements.notes: Fort at the southern end of the Volok, where hauled boats go back into the water. Its commander checks every crew against the toll-tallies sent down from Volokgrad.

settlements.name: Kosinsk
settlements.notes: Fishing village on a long sand spit, the only harbour on Borovka's short coast.

settlements.name: Lipny
settlements.notes: Bast-weavers who strip lime-tree bark for rope, shoes and sacking.

settlements.name: Lebedin
settlements.notes: Town of reed-thatched halls on piles among the Rusalka marshes, named for the swans that winter there. Strangers without a guide get lost in the reeds, which suits the townsfolk.

settlements.name: Vetlin
settlements.notes: Willow-basket weavers on the marsh edge.

settlements.name: Mokrin
settlements.notes: Eel-trappers on a sedge island; reachable on foot only in a dry summer.

settlements.name: Polynsk
settlements.notes: Steppe-edge village where Velkar farmers and Kurgai herders trade, quarrel and now and then marry.

settlements.name: Svarozhin
settlements.notes: Seat of the Dnebrava princes on a bluff above the Dnebra. The princely forge has not been let go cold in living memory, and oaths here are sworn with a hand on its anvil.

settlements.name: Vezhgrad
settlements.notes: Watch-fort over the Saryn Drag. From its timber tower the garrison can see steppe dust a day before the riders arrive.

settlements.name: Zalivny
settlements.notes: River-harbour on the lower Dnebra, the last Velkar landing above the estuary and the Kurgai shore. Dnebrava grain is loaded here into sea-boats bound for the Golden City.

settlements.name: Zhitograd
settlements.notes: Grain town on the black-earth plains. Its granaries feed half of Dnebrava and tempt every raider on the steppe.

settlements.name: Kovylny
settlements.notes: Horse-breeders on the feather-grass plain who sell remounts to the princes and, quietly, to the Kurgai.

settlements.name: Saryn
settlements.notes: Silver from the far east comes up the Sarya to be weighed and cut here. The princes of Dnebrava and the merchants of Velkgorod both claim the right to tax it.

settlements.name: Svetny
settlements.notes: Village on the forest road to Saryn, known for its fair each autumn.

settlements.name: Gromsk
settlements.notes: Hamlet on the open plain where the summer thunderstorms are fierce.

settlements.name: Kaganak
settlements.notes: The khagan's winter seat on the Ember Sea shore: felt tents ringed round a timber hall and the great horse-market. Saraleonese envoys arrive with silk every spring to keep the riders pointed at someone else.

settlements.name: Teshkala
settlements.notes: Kurgai market town on the steppe road, where horses are traded for grain, iron and salt.

settlements.name: Iltyurt
settlements.notes: Winter camp of a Kurgai clan, moved a few miles each year as the grazing gives out.

settlements.name: Bortash
settlements.notes: Herders' camp of the hereditary wardens of the old burial mounds; they do not welcome diggers.

settlements.name: Saraleon
settlements.notes: The Golden City on the Golden Strait, behind land walls older than anyone's legends. The Ember Guard holds the palace, and the sea-fire siphons of its galleys are its most closely kept secret.

settlements.name: Eudoria
settlements.notes: Vineyards and market gardens outside the land walls. Its people grumble that every army besieging Saraleon camps in their fields first.

settlements.name: Chrysopol
settlements.notes: Rich harbour city behind old imperial stone walls; its lighthouse marks the southern Ember Sea. The grain fleets for the Golden City load here.

settlements.name: Selenopol
settlements.notes: Stone-walled harbour on the western shore of the Ember Sea, the last Saraleonese city before the Corvani hills. Its governor pays the Kurgai to stay away, and pays them more every year.

settlements.name: Akrolon
settlements.notes: Hill-fort over the western road into Chryseia, garrisoned by hired horsemen whose pay is often late.

settlements.name: Hieron
settlements.notes: Fortress-town behind old imperial stone walls on the Golden Strait. Every ship that passes pays at the custom-house below its walls, and the tally-clerks are better armed than most soldiers.

settlements.name: Desmion
settlements.notes: Chain tower at the northern mouth of the Golden Strait. When its bell rings, a great iron chain is winched across the water to the Saraleon shore.

settlements.name: Myrrha
settlements.notes: Stone-walled port of perfumers and resin-merchants under the Myrrhine hills. Pirates who raid this coast sell their cargo here too, under other names.

settlements.name: Thalon
settlements.notes: Small harbour town at the tip of the Myrrhine Horn, home of sponge-divers and of the pilots who take ships through the shoals.

settlements.name: Orinthia
settlements.notes: Olive terraces and a well-guarded oil press on the Myrrhine Horn.

settlements.name: Frostgard
settlements.notes: Trading post on the Rimesea shore where Rime-hunters bring ivory, furs and eider-down to the summer ships. In winter the post is shut and the hunters go back to the ice.

settlements.name: Snaerholt
settlements.notes: Rime-hunters' camp at the edge of the Whitewaste, trading walrus ivory and seal-oil. Visitors are welcome if they bring iron.

settlements.name: Eldvik
settlements.notes: Turf houses beside a steaming bay, the first Isafolder settlement. The settlers argue about everything and talk of holding a proper Thing at the Lawstone.

sites.name: Lawstone
sites.notes: colonySite; A basalt outcrop in the hills below the Lawmere where the settlers of Eldvik say a proper Thing should one day be held. Good grazing, sheltered from the north wind.

sites.name: Askholm
sites.notes: colonySite; Turf walls of a steading abandoned after an ash-fall spoiled its hayfields, on a holm at the head of Ashfjord. The grass has long since come back.

sites.name: Brightstrand
sites.notes: colonySite; A long pale beach backed by meadow and tall timber. A ring of old hearth-stones and a fallen turf wall show that someone wintered here before.

sites.name: Mistholt
sites.notes: colonySite; A wooded vale by the Mistwater where the morning fog lies thick. A cairn of stacked stones stands at the river mouth, and nobody knows who raised it.

sites.name: the Shrine of the Iron Seed
sites.notes: Mountain shrine kept by a hermit clan of smiths who work sky-iron. A great bear dens in the crags above the only path.

sites.name: the Low-Tide Grotto
sites.notes: A sea-cave whose mouth clears only at the lowest tides of Ripening. The pearl-divers' song puts Saltha's Pearl inside.

sites.name: Cinderhollow
sites.notes: A lava tube under the eastern fells of Ashfjord; warm air breathes out of it all winter, and the floor is sharp enough to cut boots.

sites.name: the Tusk Cave
sites.notes: Sea-cave where walrus hunters cache ivory; the tide floods its lower chambers twice a day.

sites.name: the Cave of the Hundred Jars
sites.notes: Smugglers' cave in the Myrrhine hills, stacked with old wine and oil jars. Who uses it now is a question the customs-men of Myrrha would like answered.

sites.name: the Mound of the Seven Horses
sites.notes: Great steppe burial mound; the Kurgai say a khagan lies within with seven horses. Its hereditary wardens camp at Bortash.

sites.name: the Charred Hall
sites.notes: A northern traders' hall burned in a feud a generation ago. Outlaws shelter under its fallen roof-beams.

sites.name: the Wreck of the Storm-Heron
sites.notes: A broken knarr on a reef off Greenshore, proof that someone sailed west before you. Her strakes are northern work.

sites.name: the Beacon of the Nine Lamps
sites.notes: Old imperial signal tower on the heights above the Golden Strait, long unmanned; its stair is half fallen.

sites.name: the Grove of Ribbons
sites.notes: Willows on a marsh island hung with thousands of rags and ribbons, offerings to the river spirits. The Velkar take a dim view of strangers who cut them down.
